title: Method for analyzing HR-TEM micrographs to propose and/or describe structures and their interaction in crystalline materials
author: Obeso–Estrella, Pawelec, et al.
materials: All the steps performed are described bellow.

steps.title: Pretreat micrograph and filter image
steps.instruction: Select a region of the HR‑TEM micrograph, apply a Fourier Transform filter using an oval mask, adjust the ovals to the equivalent diffraction points shown in the FT image, perform the inverse transform to obtain a filtered image, optionally apply an additional Laplacian filter if the image is still unclear, and finally measure the interplanar distances on the resulting image.

steps.title: Identify phases by comparing distances
steps.instruction: Compare the measured interplanar distances with distances extracted from the ICSD database, carry out a discrimination process to select candidate structures, and simulate each candidate structure using the General Method.

steps.title: Locate three‑atom groups with similar geometry
steps.instruction: Open the two previously identified vicinal structures in Diamond software version 3.0e, display distance and angle tables via View > Table > Distances and View > Table > Angles, and visually or numerically identify sets of three atoms in each structure that have matching distances and angles; note that more than one matching triad may be found, leading to several possible connections.

steps.title: Compare modeled connection with experimental orientation
steps.instruction: Align the modeled structures with the experimental HR‑TEM micrograph, taking the zone‑axis orientation into account, to determine which atoms are plausibly involved in the structural connection.

steps.title: Create crystallographic plane through atom triad
steps.instruction: In Diamond, select the three identified atoms while holding the Ctrl key, then generate the plane that passes through them via Object > Planes > Create Plane Through Atoms… and click Accept.

steps.title: Visualize and export connected‑atom view
steps.instruction: Adjust the visualization in Diamond to obtain the clearest view of the connected atoms and, if desired, export an image or representation of the connection.

steps.title: Build chemical structure in ChemDraw
steps.instruction: Using PerkinElmer ChemDraw® version 17.0.0.206, draw the structure obtained from Diamond.

steps.title: Obtain 3D model and relax with MM2
steps.instruction: In ChemDraw, select Edit > Get 3D Model to open Chem3D, then run a molecular‑mechanics MM2 energy minimization via Calculations > MM2 > Minimize Energy… and click Run.

steps.title: Compare chemical and Diamond models
steps.instruction: Visually compare the relaxed ChemDraw 3D structure with the Diamond structural model to assess consistency between the chemical and crystallographic representations.

steps.title: Simulate TEM image with SimulaTEM
steps.instruction: Save the proposed structure as a .pdb file, load it into SimulaTEM, rotate the model until the simulated image matches the experimental HR‑TEM image, and measure interplanar distances in both simulated and experimental images to confirm the proposed structure.
